chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Hearing Duke Ellington at twelve, and Art Tatum at nineteen
summary: At black restaurants with his father he first heard Duke Ellington's orchestra, which inspired him as writer, composer and pianist; he heard Art Tatum around age 19.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: And as I said -- we were talking about who I listened to. It was during this same time also -- I didn't mention to you and I'm sure you'll be glad to hear this because of your association with him -- I was just able to get up to the juke box or the record player -- I forget what they called them at that time. But they had these machines that you put the nickel in, and my father very often took us out to dinner to keep my mother from having the chores of cooking and going to church, and preparation, which was quite hard, getting the children ready, and all the service rituals and so forth.

So to get rid of these hardships, my father very often took the family out to dinner in one of the more notable black restaurants where they had what they called home cooking. And these people were efficient in cooking good, clean, whole-

some food, and it was during that period that I used to hear the music of the famous Duke Ellington. And I was then brought into the full scope of the orchestration of jazz music, of which I became a member at the age of 12. And that is really what really started my creative mind to developing in the field of music as a pianist and orchestrator and composer. The hearing of Duke Ellington play this great music that I'd never heard before.
Strange enchantment of orchestrations and original melodies produced by all these great artists like Tricky Sam and Rex --

-- Stewart, and Cootie Williams and all these great musicians. Johnny Hodges, Lawrence Brown. All this was going through my ear and I was fascinated by it. I couldn't get it out of my system. And this is how I really started to listen to jazz music, and during that same time -- of course later on I heard Art Tatum. But much later, it was much later that I heard Art Tatum.

And I would have to say that my first inspiration came to be in the image of Duke Ellington as a writer and composer and pianist, rather than a pianist. And it was not until I heard the great artistry of Art Tatum that I knew that I wanted to become a master of ad lib playing on the piano
as well. And I was also convinced that I wasn't going to be a classical artist.
About how old were you then, do you think? Was that when you were probably a teen or --
When I heard Duke Ellington, it was all during this period when I was 12 years old.
Within the scope of a year or two, give or take as I said. And --
But when you heard Art Tatum how old were you?
I heard Art Tatum later when I was about 19. Acciently I heard him which I'll tell you about in another part of this interview when we get into that.

Because I was trying to keep this in the realm of the period from the time I was born, up until the period of around 12 and 14 when I started making decisions for myself and preparing for the day when I would leave home. Because I knew then -- I had a feeling that I would want to get out from under this regimentation, you see. I didn't know how of course.
